correctness.rationale: For all n>=2 and all r>=0, count ordered disjoint cyclic neighbor pairs via m(C_(2n),k) and uniform matching completion to obtain exact factorial moments a_(N,k). Verify their recurrence and a_(N,k)<=N/(N-1); bound the difference from 1+k(3-k)/(2N) by C(k+1)^4/N^2 uniformly over k (including k>n), which is summable with factorial weights on every fixed complex disk. The probability generating function has correction exp(z-1)(-z^2+4z-3)/(2N), and Cauchy coefficient bounds imply uniform O(n^-2 2^-r). Summing the positive correction for r=1,2,3,4 gives 73/(96en), with total error O(n^-2). Independently executed verify.py: VERIFY_OK 367 exact/reproducible assertions; finite tests only corroborate the infinite proof. Essential scopes and singular n=1 boundary explicitly addressed.

The evaluated sharp constant is not a stated corollary of those inequalities; known counting formulas are used but are not claimed new. value.rationale: The simple-chord statistic is a standard, natural test case for Poisson approximation on dependent matchings. The sharp nonzero constant quantifies the best first-order total-variation error, and a uniform signed local expansion pinpoints exactly which outcomes cause the discrepancy, including a new explicit zero-simple-chord counting correction. This supplies structurally meaningful quantitative information beyond the established O(1/n) bound and is not a merely cosmetic substitution or arbitrary finite slice.
